200 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located well north of the Papahanaumokuakea Marine
National Monument, and on Tropical Storm Moke, located a few
hundred miles south-southeast of Hilo, Hawaii.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026
 
...LALA SLIGHTLY WEAKER OVER OPEN WATERS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...32.1N 173.9W
ABOUT 335 MI...545 KM NNE OF PEARL AND HERMES ATOLL
ABOUT 365 MI...590 KM NE OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...988 MB...29.18 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was 
located near latitude 32.1 North, longitude 173.9 West. Lala has 
somewhat decelerated, and is now moving toward the west-northwest 
near 5 mph (7 km/h). This general motion is expected to continue for 
the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Gradual weakening is forecast during the next several days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 175 miles (280 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 988 mb (29.18 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Large surf associated with Lala will affect western sections
of the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument for the next
couple of days. These large waves could inundate some low-lying
atolls, especially from Maro Reef to Kure Atoll.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Mahoney/Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 45
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 231434
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  45
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026

The presentation of Tropical Storm Lala has not changed much on
infrared satellite imagery over the past six hours, with deep
convection limited to the south and eastern semicircles. Subjective
Dvorak estimates from JTWC and HFO are both T3.5/55 kt, and
objective intensity estimates are closer to 50 kt. For this
advisory, the initial intensity is lowered to 55 kt, which could be
generous but is consistent with a steady decay of the cyclone over
cooler waters.

Lala appears to have slightly decelerated on a west-northwestward 
heading (300/4 kt), as it is steered by a weak mid-level ridge 
positioned just south and east of the central Aleutian Islands. The 
tropical storm should continue on a generally west-northwestward to 
northwestward heading through the remainder of the forecast period 
as the ridge slides eastward. Lala's forward motion is not expected 
to change much, and remain somewhat slow. The track guidance this 
cycle remains in decent agreement on this scenario, though there 
continues to be some cross-track spread, with the GFS presenting a 
more eastward solution and the Google Deep Mind showing a more 
westward solution. The updated track forecast is again slightly 
slower than the previous one, and is again nudged westward toward 
the latest corrected multi-model consensus (HCCA).
 
The waters near the tropical storm are around 26C, with light shear 
and dry mid-level air. The shear and mid-level moisture are not 
likely to change much through the forecast period, so Lala should 
only weaken gradually as it moves over progressively cooler waters. 
Cooler upper tropospheric temperatures, which increase tropospheric 
instability, could counter some of the effect, at least initially, 
of the sea surface temperatures. By 120 h, Lala is forecast to 
become a post-tropical remnant low, in agreement with the GFS and 
ECMWF simulated satellite imagery and the large-scale environmental 
diagnostics from the Statistical Hurricane Intensity Prediction 
Scheme (SHIPS) guidance. The new intensity forecast is consistent 
with the previous one.

item.title: Tropical Storm Moke Public Advisory Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026 
000
WTPA33 PHFO 231443
TCPCP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Moke Advisory Number  13
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026
 
...HEAVY RAINFALL AND GUSTY WINDS EXPECTED TO SPREAD OVER THE BIG 
ISLAND OF HAWAII TODAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.2N 155.0W
ABOUT 310 MI...500 KM S OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 15 MPH...24 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Moke was
located near latitude 15.2 North, longitude 155.0 West. Moke is
moving toward the west near 15 mph (24 km/h), and this general
motion is expected to continue during the next several days. On the
forecast track, the center of the storm is expected to pass south of
the Big Island of Hawaii on Sunday, then well south of the smaller
main Hawaiian Islands early next week.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher 
gusts.  Moke is forecast to lose some strength during the next few 
days and could become a post-tropical cyclone by midweek.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles (150 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches) 
based on data from an Air Force Reserve reconnaissance aircraft.
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Tropical Storm Moke can be found in the Tropical
Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header HFOTCDCP3 and WMO header
WTPA43 PHFO.
 
WIND: Gusty winds are expected across the Hawaiian Islands during
the next couple of days, especially in areas of high terrain.
 
RAINFALL: The tropical storm is expected to produce rainfall totals
of 5 to 10 inches with maximum amounts of 15 inches across the Big
Island. Rainfall totals of 3 to 6 inches are expected on eastern
Maui. These rainfall amounts may produce life-threatening flooding
and mudslides for the windward and southeast Big Island, especially
in steep terrain and over areas that were affected recently by
Lala.
 
Across western Maui and the remainder of the islands, moisture drawn
northward from Moke may bring up to 1 or 2 inches of rain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Moke,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_cp3.shtml?rainqpf.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Moke Forecast Discussion Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026 
000
WTPA43 PHFO 231444
TCDCP3
 
Tropical Storm Moke Discussion Number  13
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026

Moke continues to pulse some convection in the northern semicircle, 
though much of the southern portion of the storm is exposed due to 
persistent shear.  The initial intensity is held at 40 kt given 
little change in the overall organization of the cyclone during the 
past several hours.  This is also in agreement with earlier 
aircraft data and close to recent Dvorak estimates.

The storm is expected to move through a challenging environment 
during the next several days, with plentiful mid-level dry air and 
moderate shear in its path.  These conditions will likely beat out 
the warm sea-surface temperatures, and Moke should struggle to 
produce sustained deep convection in this regime.  Shear is 
forecast to increase in 2-3 days, and the storm is expected to 
weaken into a tropical depression or remnant low around that time.  
The new forecast is a bit lower than the last one late in the 
period and shows an earlier transition to a post-tropical cyclone.  
It should be mentioned that more models are now showing the system 
opening up into a trough of low pressure even earlier than shown 
below due to the harsh environment and Moke's forward speed.  
 
Moke is moving westward at about 13 kt, wobbling a bit as 
convective bursts briefly pull the system north of due west.  A 
general west-northwestward motion is anticipated during the next 
several days as a strong low- to mid-level ridge remains to the 
north of the cyclone. This track should bring the center of Moke a 
couple of hundred miles south of the Big Island today and then well 
south of the rest of the main Hawaiian Islands thereafter. The 
model guidance is a bit south of the last forecast, and the NHC 
track is moved in that direction. Despite the center of Moke 
remaining south of the Hawaiian Islands, the cyclone is expected to 
pass close enough to produce a period of gusty winds and heavy 
rainfall across portions of the islands during the next couple of 
days.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Heavy rainfall associated with Tropical Storm Moke will begin to
impact the Big Island of Hawaii today. Rain will then spread 
westward across the remainder of the Hawaiian Islands through
Monday. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and
mudslides for the windward and southeast Big Island, especially in
steep terrain and over areas that were affected recently by Lala.
 
2. Although the strongest winds associated with Moke are expected to
pass south of the Hawaiian Islands, strong gusty winds are likely,
particularly in areas within and downslope of higher terrain.
